HEB-S001.extract: Hebrew: Middah (H4060). Physical context: the measured dimensions of the Tabernacle curtains (Exod 26:2). Temporal context: 'מִדַּת יָמַי' — 'the measure of my days' (Ps 39:5).
HEB-S001.notes: The same noun for architectural dimension is used explicitly for the span of a human life. BDB confirms 'once of time' at Ps 39:5.

HEB-S002.extract: Hebrew: Moed (H4150). Physical context: 'Ohel Moed' — the Tent of Meeting, a fixed place (Exod 28:43). Temporal context: 'appointed times' of the LORD (Lev 23:2).
HEB-S002.notes: Vine's notes the word carries both 'fixed time' and 'fixed place' with 'meeting' as the common denominator. The same root governs the spatial Tabernacle and the temporal feasts.

HEB-S003.extract: Hebrew: Qav (H6957). Physical context: a measuring line stretched over Jerusalem or the earth's foundations.
HEB-S003.notes: A standard architectural surveying term. No explicit temporal usage was isolated in this pass; logged as part of the measurement lexicon.

HEB-S004.extract: Hebrew: Yovel (H3104) alongside Keneh ha-Middah (H4060). The vision begins 'in the Jubilee' and the prophet is given a 'measuring rod'.
HEB-S004.notes: The 50-year time cycle (Yovel) and the architectural measuring instrument (middah) appear in the same introductory verse, linking the temporal release-cycle to the act of spatial measurement.

HEB-S005.extract: Hebrew: Amah (H520). Standard meaning: cubit, a linear measure. Lexicon adds: 'an unspecified unit of time'.
HEB-S005.notes: The cubit, the basic building block of Tabernacle and Temple dimensions, is lexically attested as a unit of time in at least one occurrence.

HEB-S006.extract: Hebrew: Shana. Root meaning 'to change, repeat'; noun: 'a year (as a revolution of time)'.
HEB-S006.notes: The year is defined lexically as a 'revolution' — a cyclical, wheel-like return. This supplies the conceptual bridge between the physical wheel (ophan/galgal) and temporal cycles.

HEB-S007.extract: Hebrew: Ophan (H212) and Galgal (H1534). The wheels of the cherubim chariot, driven by the Spirit.
HEB-S007.notes: The wheel is the explicit mechanism of the divine mobile throne. Its rotational motion provides the structural analogue for cyclical time (shana as 'revolution'). The text does not state a 5,880-year span; it supplies the wheel-image.

HEB-S008.extract: Hebrew: Chug (H2328). 'He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth.'
HEB-S008.notes: A spatial/circular term. No temporal predicate is attached in the immediate verse. Logged as part of the 'circle/wheel' lexical domain.

HEB-S009.extract: Hebrew: Mishkan (H4908). The physical 'dwelling place' constructed by Israel.
HEB-S009.notes: The primary architectural noun for the Tabernacle structure. The protocol's hypothesis requires noting that the physical dwelling (mishkan) is distinct from, though coordinated with, the appointed time (moed).

HEB-S010.extract: Hebrew: Yasad (H3245). 'To lay a foundation' of the Temple.
HEB-S010.notes: A foundation-laying verb used for the physical house of God. The temporal 'founding' or establishment of a period is not explicitly predicated with this verb in the isolated passages, but the semantic domain of 'laying a fixed base' is present.

HEB-S011.extract: Hebrew: Amah (H520). Physical context: the Ark's dimensions — 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, 30 cubits high.
HEB-S011.notes: G1: Building/measurement term present; no explicit temporal predicate in this verse. Temporal duality of amah is established separately in HEB-S005.

HEB-S012.extract: Hebrew: Tachtiyyim, Sheniyyim, Shelishiyyim (lower, second, third decks). Three-tiered internal elevation.
HEB-S012.notes: G4: The three-deck structure is interpreted as mirroring the three nested zones of later Tabernacle/Temple architecture. The text itself does not draw this connection.

HEB-S013.extract: Hebrew: Tzohar (H6672) — light opening/window, finished to a cubit (Amah).
HEB-S013.notes: G1: Architectural feature with linear measurement; no temporal predicate.

HEB-S014.extract: Hebrew: Levenim (H3843, bricks) substituted for Even (H68, stone); Chemar (H2564, asphalt) substituted for Chomer (H2563, mortar).
HEB-S014.notes: G1: Building-material terminology. No temporal predicate. Logged as part of the architectural lexicon.

HEB-S015.extract: Hebrew: Migdal (H4026, tower), Rosh (H7218, top/head), Shamayim (H8064, heavens). A city and tower with its top in the heavens.
HEB-S015.notes: G4: Interpreted as a humanly constructed spatial axis connecting earth to the cosmic realm, intended to secure a central identity (Shem). The text does not explicitly assign a temporal function.

HEB-S016.extract: Hebrew: Mo'adim (H4150). The celestial bodies are appointed 'for signs and for seasons [mo'adim]'.
HEB-S016.notes: G3: Explicit temporal use of moed. The same root governs the spatial 'Ohel Moed' (Tent of Meeting) in HEB-S002, establishing a cross-text lexical dual of time and place.

HEB-S017.extract: Hebrew: Raqia (H7549). The expanse/vault separating the waters below from the waters above.
HEB-S017.notes: G1: Structural/spatial term for the created vault. No temporal predicate in the immediate context.

HEB-S018.extract: Hebrew: Kalah (H3615) and Melakah (H4399) — verbs/nouns of completion. Creation is 'finished' (Gen 2:1-2); Moses 'finished' the work of the Mishkan (Exod 40:33).
HEB-S018.notes: G4: The verbal parallel between the completion of creation and the completion of the Tabernacle is interpreted as framing creation as a temple-building account. The text does not explicitly equate the two events.
